questions.question: When should your beacon light be on?
options: Prior to any movement and until the engines are shut down
As soon as you spawn in
questions.explanation: The beacon light indicates that engines are running or about to start.

questions.question: When are strobe lights typically turned on in Infinite Flight?
options: When entering a runway for takeoff
During the entire flight including taxi
questions.explanation: Strobes are for visibility and should be on whenever you are on an active runway.

questions.question: What is the speed limit below 10,000 feet in most airspaces?
questions.explanation: To ensure safety and traffic separation, 250kts is the standard speed limit below 10,000ft.

questions.question: Which surface on the wing is primarily used to turn the aircraft?
questions.explanation: Ailerons control the roll of the aircraft.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of flaps?
options: To increase lift and drag at lower speeds
To steer the plane on the ground
questions.explanation: Flaps allow the aircraft to fly slower while still maintaining enough lift to stay airborne.

questions.question: On the ground, what is the maximum taxi speed in Infinite Flight?
questions.explanation: Taxiing too fast (over 35kts) can result in a violation on Expert Server; 20-25kts is recommended.

questions.question: What does the ICAO airport code KJFK refer to?
questions.explanation: KJFK is John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York; the K prefix covers the contiguous United States.

questions.question: If an ATC tells you to 'Line Up and Wait', what should you do?
options: Taxi onto the runway and stop
Stay behind the hold short line
questions.explanation: This means enter the runway and wait for further takeoff clearance.

questions.question: What is 'Final' in a standard traffic pattern?
options: The leg parallel to the runway
The last leg of the approach aligned with the runway
questions.explanation: Final is the straight-in portion of the landing approach.

questions.question: What does 'Heavy' mean when added to a callsign (e.g., Speedbird 12 Heavy)?
options: The plane is carrying a lot of fuel
The aircraft has a high maximum takeoff weight
The pilot is new to the game
The plane is flying a long distance
questions.explanation: Large aircraft are designated as 'Heavy' due to the wake turbulence they create.

questions.question: When should landing gear be retracted after takeoff?
options: As soon as the wheels leave the ground
When a positive rate of climb is established
After turning off the landing lights
questions.explanation: Positive rate ensures you aren't going to sink back onto the runway.

questions.question: What color are the lights on the left wingtip?
questions.explanation: Left is Red, Right is Green.

questions.question: What is an airline's 'hub'?
options: An airport it bases flights and connections around
questions.explanation: A hub is an airport an airline concentrates its flights at, so passengers can connect between routes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Spoilers' during landing?
options: To make the plane fly faster
To reduce lift and increase drag to help the plane slow down
They have no use during landing
questions.explanation: Spoilers 'spoil' the lift and act as airbrakes.

questions.question: What is the 'Transition Altitude'?
options: The altitude at which pilots switch from local pressure (QNH) to standard pressure (1013 hPa / 29.92 inHg)
The highest altitude an aircraft can fly
The altitude where the autopilot must be engaged
The altitude where the landing gear is raised
questions.explanation: Climbing through the transition altitude, pilots set standard pressure and refer to flight levels; it varies by country.

questions.question: What is the 'Glideslope'?
options: The vertical path for a precision landing
The horizontal path to the runway
questions.explanation: The glideslope provides vertical guidance during an ILS approach.

questions.question: What should you do if you receive a 'Check Help Pages' message from ATC?
options: Review the rules/tutorials as you likely made a mistake
questions.explanation: This is a polite warning from ATC that you aren't following procedures correctly.

questions.question: Which of these aircraft is known as the 'Queen of the Skies'?
questions.explanation: The Boeing 747 earned the nickname 'Queen of the Skies'.

questions.question: What does 'V1' stand for?
options: The speed at which you must continue takeoff
questions.explanation: V1 is the 'decision speed' after which you cannot safely abort the takeoff.

questions.question: At what altitude should you usually turn off your Landing Lights when climbing?
questions.explanation: Landing lights are typically turned off passing 10,000ft.

questions.question: What is the rudder primarily used for?
options: Yaw (moving the nose left and right)
Pitch (moving the nose up and down)
questions.explanation: The rudder controls yaw, mostly used during takeoff, landing, and crosswinds.

questions.question: When following another aircraft, what is the main danger of flying too close behind them?
questions.explanation: Wake turbulence can flip or destabilize a trailing aircraft.

questions.question: In Infinite Flight, what does a 'Magenta' line on your map represent?
questions.explanation: The magenta line represents your programmed GPS path.

questions.question: What is the standard 'Unicom/CTAF' frequency used for?
options: Announcing intentions at airports without active ATC
questions.explanation: Unicom/CTAF is for pilot-to-pilot coordination at uncontrolled airports.

questions.question: What is the 'Red' area on the airspeed tape?
questions.explanation: Red indicates speeds that are dangerously fast or too slow to maintain flight.

questions.question: What is the 'APU' used for?
options: Providing power and air while engines are off
questions.explanation: The Auxiliary Power Unit provides electricity and air conditioning on the ground.

questions.question: What does the 'LNAV' button do in Infinite Flight?
options: Automatically follows your GPS flight plan
questions.explanation: Lateral Navigation (LNAV) follows the horizontal path of your flight plan.

questions.question: What is 'Short Final'?
options: The very last moments before touchdown
questions.explanation: Short final is when the aircraft is very close to the runway threshold.

questions.question: If you are flying 'East' (0-179 degrees), should your altitude usually be Even or Odd?
questions.explanation: The 'Eastbound Odd, Westbound Even' rule helps prevent mid-air collisions.

questions.question: What should you do if you are on a collision course with another aircraft?
options: Maneuver to avoid the other aircraft
questions.explanation: Safety is the priority; pilots must maneuver to avoid collisions.

questions.question: What does 'Wilco' mean in response to an ATC instruction?
questions.explanation: 'Wilco' is short for 'Will Comply.'
